div.head: II Cn 30.2
div.ab: Gyf se að þonne forðcume, ceose se man, þe þær betihtled syg, swæðer he wylle, swa anfeald ordal swa pundes weorðnc að innan þam þrim hundredan, ofer XXX peninga.
Gif se að þonne forðcume, ceose se man, þe þær betihtlad sy, swa weðer he wylle, swa anfeald ordal swa pundes weor[þ]ne að innan þam þrym hundredan, ofer þritti pænega.
Si iuramentum procedat, eligat accusatus alterutrum quod uelit, siue simplex ordalium siue iuramentum unius librę in tribus hundretis, super XXX denarios.
Gyf se að ðonne forðcume, ceose se man ðe ðær betyhtlod sy swa hwæðer swa he wylle, swa anfeald ordal swa pundes wurðne að innan ðrim hundrede, ofer XXX peninga.
Gyf se að þonne forðcume, ceose se man þe þær betihtled syg swæðer he wylle: swa anfeald ordal swa pundes weorðne að innan þam þrim hundredan ofer XXX peninga.

If the oath is forthcoming, the man who is accused there shall choose whichever he will—either the simple ordeal or an oath equivalent to a pound in value, [supported by compurgators found] within the three hundreds, [in the case of an object] over 30 pence in value.

Then, if the oath taking will proceed, the person who is accused shall there select whichever he prefers: a simple ordeal or an oath valued at one pound supported by witnesses from within the three hundreds in disputes involving property valued at more than thirty pence.

And if the oath is then forthcoming, the man who is there accused is to choose which he will have, whether simple ordeal or an oath worth a pound within the three hundreds, in a case of [stolen goods of] over 30 pence.

Wenn nun dieser Eid zu Stande kommt, dann wähle jener Mann, welcher da beschuldigt ist, eines von beiden [Reinigungsmitteln] wie er will: entweder einfaches Ordal oder einen Eid von 1 Pfund [Silbers] Werth, [mit Helfern] nicht weiter her als aus drei [dieser und zwei Nachbar-]Hundertschaften: [bei einem Object] über 30 Pfennig.

If this oath then succeeds, let the man who is accused choose whichever of the two [means of clearing himself] he wishes: either the single ordeal or an oath worth 1 pound [of silver], [with helpers] from no further away than three hundreds [this one and two neighbouring ones]: [for an object] over 30 pence.
div.note: A's ‘weor[þ]ne’ corrected by Liebermann (MS ‘weorne’). Liebermann compares I Atr 1.3.
